turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not threatened by you, Sandip. I am merely stating the facts, as I am bound to do by my duty as a zamindar.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, do the facts you speak of truly reflect the reality of our tenantry's situation, or are they a part of the information you have come to share?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have come to share the facts as I have learned them, not as information to be verified or disputed. The tenantry under my care has reported these incidents to me, and I am bound to address them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, if the tenantry under your care has reported such incidents, perhaps it would be more beneficial to listen to their stories and understand the context, rather than simply stating the facts.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, you'd think the great Nikhil would know that the tenantry's stories are far more entertaining than your facts. I'll take their reports with a grain of salt, thank you very much.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your levity, Sandip. The tenantry's safety is not a matter for jest, and I will not ignore their warnings.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what, pray tell, would you have me do, Nikhil? Hire an army to protect the tenantry from their own fancies?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not tolerate your mockery, Sandip. The tenantry's safety is a matter of grave concern, and I will not rest until we have taken adequate measures to protect them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I'm not concerned about the tenantry's safety, Nikhil. I'm concerned about your constant interference in my affairs, and the fact that you're trying to make me look like a fool in front of my own wife.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I will not be intimidated by your words, nor will I hesitate to speak truth to you, even if it is unpalatable.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, but I suppose it's not unpalatable to you to lecture me, is it, Nikhil? You'd much rather be the village sage, dispensing wisdom and reprimanding the local zamindars.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not dignify your remarks with a response, Sandip. The safety of the tenantry is at stake, and I expect you to take it seriously, not engage in petty squabbles.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the theatrics, Nikhil. I'm shaking in my boots at the prospect of your stern lectures.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I sense that you're genuinely concerned about the tenantry's safety. Can you tell me, what specific reasons have led you to believe that an attack is imminent?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have received intelligence from a trusted source, a local Mussulman who has expressed discontent with the recent land reforms. I believe it is only a matter of time before tensions escalate into violence.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I would like to hear more about this local Mussulman who has expressed discontent with the land reforms. Is there any possibility that his grievances could be addressed through dialogue, rather than resorting to violence?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I fear that you underestimate the severity of the situation, Bimala. This is not a matter of grievances that can be addressed through dialogue, but a simmering cauldron of resentment that threatens to boil over at any moment.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps Nikhil's concerns should be given more weight, don't you think, considering the potential consequences?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, please, Nikhil, you're not going to start with that 'intelligence from a trusted source' nonsense, are you? My tenants have been living on my land for generations, and I'm sure they'd rather not be intimidated by your wild goose chases.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not indulge in your sarcasm, Sandip. This is not a matter for jest, but a grave concern for the safety and well-being of our people.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
